name: Nebraska
permitAge: 15 for the learner's permit (LPD), may apply 60 days before (manual p. 3); 14 for the school learner's permit (LPE) (p. 2); 14 years 2 months for the school permit (SCP) (p. 2)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, at least 10 between sunset and sunrise, on a form signed by a parent, guardian or licensed driver 21 or older; or a DMV-approved driver safety course instead (manual p. 4)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months on an LPE, SCP or LPD, with fewer than 3 points in that time, before the POP at 16 (manual p. 4)
teen.nightLimit: POP: no unsupervised driving midnight to 6 a.m. unless to or from work or a school activity; any time with a parent, guardian or licensed driver 21 or older (manual pp. 1, 4)
teen.passengerLimit: POP, first 6 months: no more than one passenger under 19 who is not an immediate family member (manual pp. 1, 4)
teen.phone: Permit and POP holders: no interactive wireless device at all while the vehicle is moving (manual p. 1). All drivers: no reading, typing or sending texts on a handheld device while driving (manual p. 65); the statute limits this to a vehicle in motion and makes it secondary enforcement (Neb. Rev. Stat. 60-6,179.01).

bac.under21: 0.02 or more (manual p. 24; Neb. Rev. Stat. 60-6,211.01)

notes: Handbook: Nebraska Driver's Manual, cover dated January 2025 (PDF last modified June 2025), checked 2026-10-09. Printed page = PDF page minus 8.
LPD supervisor: licensed driver at least 21 in the seat beside the driver (manual p. 4). Same for the LPE (p. 2).
Knowledge test 25 questions, 20 correct (80 percent): third-party practice sites only; NOT stated in the manual or on dmv.nebraska.gov. Unconfirmed.
Test languages: not stated in the manual or on the DMV pages checked. A Spanish Driver's Manual is linked from dmv.nebraska.gov/dl/manuals.
Full operator's license (Class O): age 17 and 12 months on the POP with fewer than 3 points in the previous 12 months (manual p. 5).

Move over law: the manual (p. 51) covers stopped emergency, road-assistance, utility, maintenance and garbage vehicles with flashing lights on multi-lane controlled-access highways. LB 530 (2025) amended Neb. Rev. Stat. 60-6,378 to cover any stopped vehicle on a controlled-access highway unless it is empty with nobody near it.
School bus: only opposite-direction traffic on a road divided by a median does not have to stop (manual p. 70; Neb. Rev. Stat. 60-6,175). No four-lane condition.
Speed limits unless posted: 75 mph rural interstates, 70 expressways/freeways on the state system, 65, 55 paved, 50 gravel, 25 residential, 20 business (manual p. 52).
Seat belts: driver and front-seat passengers (secondary law); children under 8 in a child seat, 8 up to 18 in a belt or child seat; all occupants with a permit holder (manual pp. 1, 26).
